title: Read exact Project category configuration without inventing budget authority

requirements.invariant: Later Project budget progress groups canonical paid and unpaid contributions by stable Project category without double counting. This configuration slice preserves category selection/allocation context only and cannot calculate, cache or alter any contribution or spend value.

For every visible stable category, Project configuration distinguishes no relationship, enabled without allocation, enabled with explicit zero Money and enabled with positive Money. Every supplied allocation is exact non-negative integer-currency Money; absent, null and zero never collapse.

requirements.section: Security and Sync Requirements for Later Target Mapping
requirements.invariant: The local snapshot contains only category definitions and allocation values already authorized for the Principal in the exact Account and Project. It does not perform authorization or reveal hidden category/allocation rows or counts; incomplete relationship evidence remains explicit rather than becoming no relationship.

A monotonic Project configuration revision and immutable read evidence prepare later conflict-aware complete-set updates, but this slice exposes no ConfigureProjectCategories command and no shared category Create/Update/Archive/Reorder operation while O-026 remains open.

Project category configuration is an immutable local read model with exact Account/Project query identity, LocalDataVersion, readiness/quality, visible-row count and as-of evidence. Authorized empty, incomplete, partial and stale local scope remain distinct and reconstruct only through the same validators.

requirements.section: Clients, Projects, notes, preferences, and reference data
requirements.invariant: One narrow backend-neutral Project-category configuration query port exposes exact Account/Project-scoped local snapshots using domain and standard Swift types only; it contains no generic CRUD, provider listener, authorization implementation or backend SDK type.

This Phase 1 read boundary is executable only with deterministic provider-free evidence while the shipped app remains unchanged and no Project allocation table, RLS policy, Sync Stream, Auth/provider choice, source transform, hosted resource or production authority is introduced.

items: ProjectCategoryConfigurationState has exactly noRelationship, enabledWithoutAllocation, enabledWithAllocation(Money) and relationshipEvidenceIncomplete. Only enabledWithAllocation carries exact non-negative Money; explicit zero remains a carried value.

ProjectCategoryConfigurationRow binds one verified BudgetCategoryDefinitionSnapshot to one configuration state. Archived/system definitions may remain visible for historical configuration evidence but their existing eligibility values do not grant selection or mutation authority.

ProjectCategoryConfigurationSnapshot binds one AccountID, ProjectID and configuration revision to the shared validated ListLocalSnapshot contract, refuses duplicate category identity/name/order and treats visibleRowCountBeforeFiltering as the already-authorized visible count only.

No-relationship is accepted only when relationship evidence is complete; relationshipEvidenceIncomplete is accepted only when it is incomplete. Present enabled evidence may remain visible in partial/stale snapshots without claiming the missing working set.

ProjectCategoryConfigurationQuerying exposes only watchProjectCategoryConfiguration(accountId:projectId:) local streams; ProjectCategoryConfigurationFailure provides stable safe state/scope/duplicate/readiness/request codes.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: This Phase 1 provider-free contract creates no Project-category relation, category table, column, check, unique constraint, index, view or migration; the complete target vertical slice must define those after applicable gates.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: No ConfigureProjectCategories or shared category administration command, transaction, lock, idempotency result or server read handler is implemented; O-026 remains open.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No relation, view or function is exposed through the Supabase Data API.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: Account/Project/value validation and already-authorized subset shape are not authorization. No server rows, membership/financial-visibility predicate, grants or RLS policies exist in this slice.

syncStreams.notApplicable: The read port consumes local snapshots but defines no PowerSync Stream, bucket parameter, local table, financial-visibility download rule or provider readiness proof.

items: Configuration state, rows and snapshots are immutable Codable evidence and reconstruct only through the same category, allocation, Account, Project, identity, order and readiness validators.

The shared ListLocalSnapshot contract retains query fingerprint, bounded already-authorized rows/count, completeness, ready/partial/stale quality, LocalDataVersion and canonical as-of time across restart.

Cross-Account categories, duplicate category IDs/names/orders, invalid negative allocation, no-relationship from incomplete evidence and incomplete markers in complete evidence fail atomically without returning a partial configuration snapshot.

storageMedia.notApplicable: Project category configuration contains no image URL, AttachmentPath, byte reference, cache, upload, retention or deletion behavior.

appMcp.notApplicable: The shared read values and port semantics are defined, but no concrete Swift form/context, MCP TypeScript projection, transport handler, capability registration or entry point is wired in this foundation slice.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No Firebase allocation/category/Fee/budget-summary row is transformed and no absent/null/zero variant is repaired. Later migration must admit or quarantine every source configuration explicitly.

observabilityRunbooks.notApplicable: Stable local failure codes are contract values only; no telemetry emission, metric, alert or runbook action is added.

items: The implementation remains inside the existing provider-free LedgerTargetCore and test targets and is not linked by changing either application project.
This slice cannot activate Project configuration, authorize financial values, mutate categories/allocations, calculate budgets, provision a database, import source data, deploy, release or cut over.

verification.expected: Valid synthetic visible rows preserve exact Account/Project/category identity, no-relationship/enabled-null/enabled-zero/enabled-positive state, category definition evidence and configuration revision without budget arithmetic, authorization or provider dependencies.

Ready, partial, stale and authoritative-empty authorized snapshots round-trip byte-identically with stable category order, exact relationship-known/incomplete truth, query fingerprint, configuration revision, LocalDataVersion and as-of evidence.

Negative/malformed allocation, cross-Account category, duplicate ID/name/order, hidden-count mismatch, no-relationship from incomplete evidence, incomplete marker in complete evidence and malformed decoded values fail atomically through stable configuration codes.
A deterministic reference port returns only the exact Account/Project snapshot, refuses mismatched Account or Project requests without yielding rows and a failing port yields no false snapshot.

verification.owner: pull-request CI Isolated target environment job
verification.expected: The exact implementation commit passes conversion traceability, provider/source-contamination and generated-contract checks, the complete target suite, both target builds and clean artifacts without changing an application project or claiming budget, server, authorization, provider, migration or production behavior.

notes: Decision-independent Phase 1 authorized-read contract only. O-026 remains fully open because no category definition/order or Project configuration mutation exists. Financial visibility is modeled as an already-authorized visible subset and is not decided locally. The slice stops before budget contribution calculation, physical durable storage, server/download authorization, schema/RLS/Sync/Auth/provider, app/MCP, source migration, hosted resources, production access or cutover.
